# Results — Study 887 (High-Yield Muni Premium)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **high-yield
municipal bonds pay a fat, tax-advantaged credit spread over investment-grade munis** — run live
on the actual packaged vehicles: **HYD vs MUB/TFI** (the HY-muni credit premium), **HYG** as the
taxable-HY yardstick for the tax-equivalent-yield comparison, **BIL** as the tradable risk-free.
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
The sample is frozen as-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month
is dropped). Fingerprint `db0172501766`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily auto-adjusted (**total-return, net-of-fee**) closes — HYD, MUB, TFI, HYG, BIL (public, no key); a second price-only pull backs out the tax-relevant income (distribution) leg |
| Window | panel 2007-04-11 → 2026-06-30 (4,836 days); HYD-era common monthly sample **2009-03 → 2026-06 (208 months, 17.3 yrs)** |
| Risk-free | **BIL** (1-3m T-bill ETF) — every Sharpe race is **excess-vs-excess** on a tradable rf |
| Execution lag | one, documented: HYD lists 2009-02; the MUB→HYD switch executes at a month-end close and returns accrue the following month — no same-bar fill, no partial listing month |
| Costs | one-way bps × NAV on each leg of the single MUB→HYD switch; long-only, no shorts, no borrow; ETF fees (HYD 0.35%, MUB 0.05%, TFI 0.23%, HYG 0.49%) already inside the net-of-fee tape |
| Tax convention | top-bracket federal marginal rate **40.8%** (37% + 3.8% NIIT); muni coupon income tax-exempt, taxable-HY (HYG) income taxed at that rate; price appreciation left pre-tax for both |

## Headline — the HY-muni credit spread, HYD − MUB

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| monthly spread HYD − MUB | **+20.21 bps/mo** · HAC (Newey-West) *t* = **+1.80** (n = 208, lags = 4) |
| bootstrap mean 95% CI | **[−1.44, +42.23] bps/mo** · frac < 0 = 3.6% (block = 6) — **the interval touches zero** |
| annualised total return | HYD **5.38%/yr** vs MUB **3.20%/yr** → spread **+2.43 pp/yr** (TFI 3.01%, HYG 7.26%, BIL 1.25%) |
| excess Sharpe (rf = BIL) | HYD **0.478** vs MUB **0.408** vs TFI **0.341** — HYD advantage over MUB **+0.069** |

The HY-muni fund has out-earned the IG-muni benchmark by **+2.43 pp/yr for 17.3 years** — but the
monthly spread **does not clear the desk bar**: HAC *t* = **1.80** (< 2) and the bootstrap 95% mean
CI **includes zero**. The excess-Sharpe advantage over MUB is real but thin (**+0.07**).

## Era cut + the crisis windows (where illiquidity bites)

| window | spread (bps/mo) | HAC *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2009-2016 | +27.4 | +1.85 | 94 |
| 2017-2026 | +14.3 | +0.91 | 114 |
| **2020 COVID** | **−18.4** | −0.15 | 12 |
| **2022 rate shock** | **−78.0** | **−4.35** | 12 |

Neither sub-era clears *t* = 2 on its own (2009-2016 *t* = 1.85; 2017-2026 *t* = 0.91). And the
premium **inverts violently in stress**: in 2022 HY-muni *lost* to IG-muni by **−78 bps/mo** at HAC
*t* = **−4.35** — the illiquidity that bites in crises, exactly as the claim warns. The Sharpe
advantage over MUB is at least *sign-consistent* across halves (**+0.13** in 2009-2017, **+0.15** in
2018-2026), which is why the Signal is Weak rather than None.

## The tax wrapper — where the real edge lives

Muni coupons are federally tax-exempt; the income (distribution) leg is measured directly as
total-return minus price-return.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| income (distribution) yield | HYD **5.43%/yr** · MUB 2.71% · HYG 6.04% |
| HYD **tax-equivalent yield** @ 40.8% | **9.17%** vs taxable HYG **6.04%** |
| after-tax annualised total return | HYD **5.38%** vs HYG **4.67%** vs MUB 3.20% |
| after-tax excess Sharpe (rf = BIL after tax) | HYD **0.53** · MUB **0.51** · HYG **0.50** |

This is the genuinely positive, mechanical finding. On a pre-tax basis taxable HY (HYG, 7.26%/yr)
buries HY-muni (5.38%/yr). **After tax the ranking flips**: HYD's tax-equivalent yield is **9.17%**
vs HYG's **6.04%**, and HYD's after-tax total return (**5.38%**) tops HYG's (**4.67%**). But the
after-tax *risk-adjusted* races are a near-tie (HYD 0.53 vs HYG 0.50 vs MUB 0.51) — the wrapper makes
HY-muni *competitive*, it does not manufacture a robust Sharpe edge. And it only accrues to a
top-bracket investor holding in a *taxable* account.

## Risk — the price of admission

| vehicle | max drawdown (daily total-return, 2009-02 →) |
|---|--:|
| HYD | **−35.6%** (2020-02-26 → 2020-03-18) |
| MUB | **−13.7%** (2020-03-09 → 2020-03-19) |
| HYG | −22.0% (2020-02-13 → 2020-03-23) |

HY-muni's COVID crash is **22 pp deeper** than IG-muni's and deeper even than taxable HY's — the thin
muni-HY market gaps hard when liquidity vanishes. You are paid the spread partly *for* wearing this.

## Costs — one switch, negligible drag

The trade is a single long-only substitution (sell MUB, buy HYD) held for the sample. One-way cost ×
NAV on each of the 2 legs, amortised over 17.3 years; gross spread +243 bps/yr:

| one-way cost | drag (bps/yr) | net spread (bps/yr) |
|---|--:|--:|
| 5 bps | 0.6 | **+242** |
| 15 bps | 1.7 | **+241** |
| 30 bps | 3.5 | **+239** |

Friction on the *switch* is invisible — costs do not erase the edge. What erases confidence in it is
the thin *t*, the zero-touching CI, and the crisis inversion, not the trading bill.

## Synthetic control — machinery proof (never market evidence)

A deterministic world where HYD = premium + 1.15·MUB + noise, with a **planted** annual premium knob:

| planted premium | mean (bps/mo) | HAC *t* | bootstrap 95% CI | frac < 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.0%/yr (null)** | +5.18 | +1.13 | [−3.5, +14.1] | 0.128 |
| **+3.0%/yr** | +30.18 | +6.59 | [+21.5, +39.1] | 0.000 |

With zero planted premium the pipeline stays under *t* = 2 and its CI includes zero (it does not
manufacture significance); a planted +3%/yr lights up at *t* ≈ 6.6 with a CI clear of zero. The
HAC/bootstrap machinery is faithful. *(A machinery proof only — never cited in support of a stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The HY-muni credit spread is positive and economically large (**+20.21 bps/mo,
  +2.43 pp/yr** over 17.3 years) and the excess-Sharpe advantage over MUB is sign-consistent across
  halves (**+0.07** full, +0.13 / +0.15 by half) — but it **fails the robust bar**: HAC *t* = **1.80**
  (< 2), the bootstrap 95% mean CI **[−1.44, +42.23]** touches zero, neither sub-era clears *t* = 2,
  and the premium **inverts to −78 bps/mo (*t* = −4.35) in the 2022 crisis**. Directionally real,
  statistically thin, crisis-fragile → Weak, not Real (and not None: the sign is right).
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Costs do *not* kill it — the one-switch hold drags ≤ **3.5 bps/yr** vs a
  **+239 bps/yr net** spread, fees inside the tape — so this is **not** a Mirage. It is Fragile: the
  underlying Signal is thin and does not robustly clear; the payoff is crisis-fragile (**−35.6% vs
  −13.7%** COVID drawdown; the spread goes deeply negative in stress); and the one genuinely
  mechanical pickup — the **tax wrapper** (TEY **9.17%** vs **6.04%**, after-tax HYD **5.38%** > HYG
  **4.67%**) — only accrues to a top-bracket investor in a taxable account and leaves the after-tax
  *risk-adjusted* race a near-tie (0.53 vs 0.50).
- **"A paid credit premium in a tax-favored wrapper?" — HALF TRUE.** The *wrapper* is real and
  mechanical (muni coupons are tax-exempt by law; TEY 9.2% vs 6.0% is arithmetic). The *credit
  premium over IG munis* is the part that does not certify: +2.4 pp/yr gross, but *t* = 1.80, CI to
  zero, and a −78 bps/mo 2022 inversion. Buy HY-muni for the tax-equivalent yield if you are
  top-bracket and taxable — not for a robust, all-weather HY-over-IG-muni credit edge.
